paragraphs: The ADK-Powered Travel Planner is a multi-agent travel-planning application. A host service coordinates specialist services for flights, stays, and activities, while a Streamlit UI provides the user-facing workflow.
Generated flights, stays, and activities are illustrative suggestions only; they are not live availability, live prices, or bookable offers.

Documentation: the full docs are a Mintlify site in docs/, organized as tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation. New here? Start with the tutorial, docs/tutorials/first-trip-plan.mdx. To browse the site locally, install the CLI (npm i -g mint), then run mint dev in docs/ and open
features: Multi-Agent Architecture: Orchestrates specialized agents for different travel aspects.
Pluggable LLM Provider: Ollama (Meta Llama, self-hosted) or OpenAI gpt-4o-mini (cloud), selected by LLMPROVIDER.
Structured Responses: Requests JSON-schema-constrained output from either provider and validates it against shared Pydantic contracts.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Flight, Stay, and Activities add relevant Wikivoyage passages to their prompts, retrieved with LlamaIndex (from Chroma when self-hosted, or a committed file index on Vercel), and trip…
Containerized Runtime: One Dockerfile with separate API and UI images, so each installs only the dependencies it needs.

requirements.text: Project status: the self-hosted setup is the supported way to run the project.
npm i -g vercel, vercel login, then vercel link --yes --project travel-planner from the repository root.
The Host API key is what clients must send as X-API-Key; generate a long random value.
Any other client must send the key too, for example curl -H "X-API-Key: " -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @trip.json /run.
If your AWS CLI signs in with aws login, run eval "$(aws configure export-credentials --format env)" in the same shell before each Terraform command; Terraform can't read those credentials directly.
